# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mrs. Rachel  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Rachel Lynde  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a fat woman who walks with a waddle. She has a sharp, all-seeing eye that carefully observes everything passing by her window.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken, opinionated woman who prides herself on always speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly capable and industrious, she manages her own household efficiently while closely attending to her neighbors' affairs out of intense curiosity. Although she can be pessimistic, critical, and tactless regarding others' appearances and choices, she possesses a kindly, warm heart, shows genuine sympathy in times of trouble, and is willing to admit her mistakes when proven wrong.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P22](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0022), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P28](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0028), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c10 P38](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0038)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables, where she kept a watchful eye on all Avonlea happenings. Upon discovering that Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert planned to adopt an orphan boy, she voiced her strong disapproval, and was further astonished when Matthew brought home a girl, Anne Shirley, instead. During her first visit to inspect the child, Mrs. Rachel insulted Anne's appearance, provoking an explosive outburst from the girl. After Anne delivered a humble apology, Mrs. Rachel forgave her and grew quite fond of her over time. Throughout Anne's upbringing, Mrs. Rachel frequently offered unsolicited advice on her discipline and education, recommending that Marilla humor Anne's reluctance to attend school after an incident with Mr. Phillips. She attended a political rally in Charlottetown as a staunch Liberal, accompanied by her husband and Marilla. Later, she helped organize local events such as the Avonlea Debating Club library concert and the Church Aid bazaars.

## Quotes

> There are plenty of people, in Avonlea and out of it, who can attend closely to their neighbors' business by dint of neglecting their own; but Mrs. Rachel Lynde was one of those capable creatures who can manage their own concerns and those of other folks into the bargain.  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

> I’m clean puzzled, that’s what, and I won’t know a minute’s peace of mind or conscience until I know what has taken Matthew Cuthbert out of Avonlea today.  <sub>[v1 c1 P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005)</sub>

> Well, Marilla, I’ll just tell you plain that I think you’re doing a mighty foolish thing—a risky thing, that’s what.  <sub>[v1 c1 P25](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0025)</sub>

> Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.  <sub>[v1 c13 P19](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0019)</sub>

> If you can’t be cheerful, be as cheerful as you can.  <sub>[v1 c32 P5](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0005)</sub>
